name: Auslan
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible
sweep_summary: Auslan (aust1271) is not in the catalog and is a signed language, so spoken-language word-stress position does not apply. The only works with stress in the title, Hodge, Ferrara & Johnston 2011 'Using prosody and grammar to describe natural discourse in Auslan', is an unpublished talk at DGfS 2011 AG 6 (signed-language text linguistics), confirmed from the archived workshop programme; no abstract or text is obtainable ( never archived, live site 404, no Crossref/ORCID record). It concerns discourse-level prosodic boundary cues, not word stress. Its descendant, Hodge 2013 PhD (held by the project, was read and contains no lexical stress statement for Auslan (p. 23: 'There has been very little research on prosodic structure in Auslan'). No first-hand stress statement found; nothing to acquire.

sources.citation: Hodge, Gabrielle. 2013 [deposited 2014]. Patterns from a signed language corpus: clause-like units in Auslan (Australian sign language). PhD thesis, Macquarie University. doi:10.25949/19442855.v1
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on lexical/word stress placement. Ch. 2 (pp. ~25-31 of the text) reviews signed-language prosody in the Prosodic Phonology hierarchy (Intonational Phrase boundaries, blinks, holds, rhythm; cites Wilbur 1999 'Stress in ASL') and notes 'several studies on several different signed languages have failed to identify a single prominent marking strategy of signed language prosody'; the thesis works at the clause/intonation-unit level only.
